name: The Meridian Underground Railroad
description: Not a single vehicle but a secret network of maintained tunnels, hidden rail lines, safe houses, and improvised transport that moves people — refugees, escapees, the disappeared — through the Underworld from one side of GLMZ to the other without surfacing. The Railroad uses everything: mining carts, rafts, crawlers, walking paths, and passages that shouldn't exist. It has been operating for at least thirty years. No one knows who runs it. The name is deliberate, historical, and weighted with meaning.
propulsion: Various — whatever the network provides at each segment
speed: Variable. A full transit takes 8-16 hours.
tier_availability: By invitation only. You don't find the Railroad — it finds you.
cost: Free. The Railroad doesn't charge. It asks you to help the next person.
autonomy: Human-guided throughout. Trust is the navigation system.
armament: Whatever the guides carry. Anonymity is the primary defense.
common_usage: Escaping corporate indenture, fleeing security sweeps, relocating threatened individuals, disappearing.
story_hooks: A freelancer is asked to escort someone through the Railroad and discovers it passes through chambers that contain technology from before the city was founded
The Railroad's operators are being hunted by a corporate AI that has learned to predict their routes — and someone inside is feeding it data
physical_description: The Meridian Underground Railroad exists as a labyrinthine network rather than a discrete object—corroded steel rails buried beneath decades of sediment, concrete passages reinforced with salvaged industrial framework, and wooden support structures darkened by mineral seepage and age. Weathered signage, hand-painted route markers, and jury-rigged lighting systems (salvaged neon tubes, oil lamps, bioluminescent fungi in some sections) guide travelers through tunnels that smell of rust, water, and earth. The infrastructure bears the scars of thirty years: graffiti memorials, makeshift stations carved into bedrock, and countless repair patches welded onto failing infrastructure by anonymous hands.
